site.name: Riverside Mixed Development, Millbrook
site.description: Fictional site investigation for a mixed-use riverside development. 16 boreholes drilled to 15-20m depth across a 250×200m area.

geological_units.name: Made Ground
geological_units.description: Variable fill material including demolition rubble, ash, and reworked natural soils. Loose to medium dense. Encountered across most of the site reflecting historical industrial use.
geological_units.engineering_notes: Variable compressibility. Not suitable as founding stratum without treatment.

geological_units.name: River Terrace Deposits
geological_units.description: Medium dense to dense, sub-angular to sub-rounded flint GRAVEL with coarse sand. Occasional cobbles. Thickness increases toward the eastern boundary.
geological_units.engineering_notes: Good founding stratum. SPT N values typically 25-45.

geological_units.name: Alluvial Clay
geological_units.description: Soft to firm, dark grey, silty CLAY with occasional organic laminae and shell fragments. High plasticity. Lens-like geometry controlled by former river channel.
geological_units.engineering_notes: Consolidation settlement risk. Cu typically 20-40 kPa. Su(rem) low.

geological_units.name: Chalk
geological_units.description: Soft to medium hard, white to light grey CHALK, Grade B/C (structurally weak to medium). Fractured in upper 2m. Slight flint bands at depth. Consistent across site.
geological_units.engineering_notes: Check for solution features. SPT refusal common below 1.5m. Good long-term founding stratum.
